thread:
Jules: Quick flag — telemetry shows a subset of tenants with flat token usage but a sudden drop in model-quality metrics. Thinking about tying adaptive token refill to downstream quality signals. Thoughts?
Nina: Interesting. You mean boost burst allowance for tenants with good quality, and throttle those with regressions?
Jules: Exactly. Idea: quality_multiplier * base_refill where quality_multiplier derived from rolling evals (0.5..2.0).
Alex: Uh, risk of gaming. Tenants could craft prompts that look good to our evals but are harmful otherwise.
Priya: Also privacy concern if quality signals come from user content. We should only use aggregated metrics (eval-sample scores, reject-rate, nlu-flags) and avoid storing raw text.
Nina: Agreed on aggregation. We can feed sampled eval-scores from production samplers (1/1000) into the refill calc.
Jules: Perf note: the refill path must be cheap. Prefer a background aggregator that publishes per-tenant score every minute, not per-request compute.
Alex: That pushes us towards a leaky-bucket style refill with time-varying rate, not a token-bucket where we mutate burst per request. Simpler to reason about.
Priya: Implementation-wise: keep refill-rate = clamp(base * quality_mul, min, max). Keep burst window independent and small.
Jules: Sketch config block: 
```
refill_policy:
  mode: leaky
  window: 60s
  min_rate: 0.5
  max_rate: 10
  quality_multiplier_source: eval-aggregator-v2
```
Nina: We should also think fairness: small tenants shouldn't be starved because large ones optimize quality metric collection. Maybe add a per-tenant floor and a cross-tenant equity cap.
Alex: Equity cap sounds right. Also need to define update cadence and smoothing to avoid oscillation (EWMA with alpha=0.2?).
Priya: Security: do not accept external-signed quality tokens. Only internal aggregator publishes signed quality manifests. Log provenance_token for audits.
ops-bot: Incident: created ticket #IN-8315 to alert when adaptive-refill changes cause >5% latency regression for top-50 tenants.
kb-bot: Docs: https://internal/redwood/docs/adaptive-refill (draft) — added a short primer.
Jules: Monitoring: Nina can we surface a "quality->refill" delta in console per-tenant so customers can see why refill changed?
Nina: Yes, we can add a read-only panel showing last_quality, applied_mul, base_rate, final_rate. Need metrics emitted by policy service.
Alex: On abuse angle: if refill correlates with quality, malicious actors could pump quality scores then flood. Suggest probation windows and ramping for newly-increased refill.
Priya: Probation policy: when quality_mul increases >x% in a single window, cap burst for first 10 minutes and require stable improvement.
Jules: Good. Also add audit-replay: sample decisions and recompute quality offline to detect drift/poisoning.
Nina: Can add replay job that runs hourly on 0.1% sample, emits mismatch rate.
Alex: Performance target: refill decision propagation <= 30s from aggregator publish. Otherwise it's stale.
Priya: Privacy action: anonymize tenant-sample ids, store only aggregates, retention 30d, and redaction for PII.
Jules: Action items: I'll draft RFC with config examples and threat model. Nina will spec dashboard panels and replay job. Alex will prototype smoothing parameters and equity cap math. Priya will write privacy constraints.
ops-bot: Deploy plan: feature-flagged behind `adaptive_refill_v1`, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%.
Jules: Target RFC EOW. Ping me for pairing. :rocket:
